rationale:
structural: The requirement prescribes two structural items in the `Domain` trait. The first is the associated type `type NodeContent: NodeContents;`. The second is the method `fn node_content(&self, node: &NodeId<Self>) -> Result<Self::NodeContent, Self::Error>;`. The clauses are "as values implementing `NodeContents`" and "failures return the domain's error". An alternative that returned an unbounded type, or a different error type, would break these clauses even if the runtime results were the same. Both items therefore need implementation evidence.

The two review roots are `crates/trust-but-verify/src/domain.rs#trait[Domain]/type[NodeContent]` and `crates/trust-but-verify/src/domain.rs#trait[Domain]/fn[node_content]`. I read both declarations. The type has the `NodeContents` bound. The method takes `&self` and `&NodeId<Self>` and returns `Result<Self::NodeContent, Self::Error>`. Each root carries an `{impl}` marker for the requirement. The requirement says reading includes loading and preparation, and the doc comment on `node_content` says the same. That part describes behavior of each domain's implementation, which tests cover. It is not a separate structural obligation. Every structural obligation is covered by the two roots, so there is no gap.

behavioral: Obligations derived from `requirements.sdk.graph.node_content`: (1) `Domain::node_content` reads a node as a `NodeContents` value; (2) reading includes the loading and preparation needed to fingerprint and format the value; (3) failures return the domain's own error. The fingerprint and format detail is in the refining `.fingerprint` and `.format` requirements, so it is not reassessed here.

- Returning content: `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[identities_remain_stable_and_fingerprinting_uses_the_supplied_snapshot]` reads a node and asserts `snapshot.content.format()` is "before". It asserts the fingerprint value is "before", and that the content's fingerprint equals the snapshot fingerprint after the underlying data changes. `src/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[requirement_edges_and_input_freshness_use_the_sdk]` calls `domain.node_content` on a real `HabeasDomain` selector node and asserts the fingerprint equals the retained one. It also checks that the content changes after the file changes.
- Loading and preparation failures: `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[queued_reads_selection_and_rendering_fail_before_agent_invocation]` sets `fail_read` and asserts `ValidationError::Graph("read")`. It then sets `fail_prepare` and asserts `Graph("render")`. In the `Memory` domain's `node_content`, both errors are returned from `node_content` itself, so preparation failure is reported at read time. It also asserts no dependencies are recorded and no agent call is made.
- Domain error propagation: `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[wildcard_versions_still_check_inputs_and_errors]` sets `fail_read` and asserts `record.is_current` returns exactly `Err("read")`. The domain's error therefore passes through unchanged.

I found no obligation without a test, and no assertion that contradicts the requirement. The trait signature itself is structural.
